patterns_detected.description: Full-text search using PostgreSQL tsvector/tsquery operators or MySQL MATCH AGAINST. OpenSearch's inverted index is purpose-built for this workload: tokenization, stemming, and relevance ranking are native.
LIKE/ILIKE wildcard queries on text columns. OpenSearch wildcard queries are more scalable than SQL LIKE on large datasets, with no full-table scan.
Regex pattern matching (REGEXP, RLIKE, PostgreSQL ~ operator). OpenSearch supports regexp queries with finite automaton execution, avoiding full-scan overhead.
Range queries on timestamp columns (created_at, event_time, etc.). OpenSearch time-series indices with date histograms excel at this access pattern.
Time-based aggregations using DATE_TRUNC, DATE(), HOUR(), or EXTRACT(). OpenSearch date histogram aggregations run against pre-sorted time fields, which is very efficient.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Queries joining multiple tables (join_count >= 2). OpenSearch has no join across indexes: nested documents and the join field type relate documents inside one index only, so the data must be denormalized into one index or joined in the application layer (OpenSearch documentation, Joining queries).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Denormalize into a single OpenSearch index, or handle joins in the application layer by fetching related documents separately.
